basis: Inherited bile-acid homeostasis disorder causes progressive liver failure; characteristic vitamin-K-independent coagulopathy with prolonged PT occurs in 4/4.
Inherited factor X deficiency impairs coagulation; bleeding sites do not establish additional organ damage.
Deletion syndrome associated with developmental and speech impairment; supplied record lacks clinical detail supporting additional axes.
Developmental speech-fluency disorder affecting neurologic speech production.
Inclusion-body myopathy and Paget bone disease define this subtype; dementia is optional and not established as common in the supplied cohort.
Premature loss of ovarian endocrine function with elevated gonadotropins; other FMR1-associated disorders are separate conditions.
Congenital abnormal artery-to-vein connection; skin ulceration and other organ complications are not established as common across the group.
Fibro-osseous bone lesions define disease; FGF23-mediated hypophosphatemia is annotated frequent (30-79%), supporting metabolic involvement.
Microcephaly, seizures and cortical visual impairment define CNS disease; optic atrophy occurs in 3/4. Bronchiectasis (1/4) and immunodeficiency are below threshold.
Posterior corneal stromal and Descemet membrane opacities impair vision.
Fibrosis directly affects bile ducts, which belong to the hepatic axis.
Isolated spermatogenic failure causes male infertility; no hormonal failure or systemic metabolic disease is established.
Developmental impairment, callosal agenesis and seizures define disease; strabismus and cardiac septal abnormalities each occur in 30-79%. Renal abnormalities are occasional.
Inherited circadian sleep-wake timing disorder; associated depression has no organ axis.
Infantile autophagic vacuolar skeletal myopathy; cardiomyopathy and developmental delay are reported, but their frequency and diagnostic status are insufficiently established.
Skeletal dysplasia; respiratory insufficiency in 8/8 and renal phosphate wasting with hypophosphatemia in 5/6 support additional axes. Proptosis alone does not establish eye damage.
Inherited circadian sleep-wake timing disorder; associated migraine also falls within the neurologic axis.
Hereditary macular dystrophy affects the retina; both listed parental disease groups are ocular.
Developmental deformity of sternum and chest wall; clinically significant cardiac or pulmonary impairment is not established in at least 30% overall.
Adenocarcinoma originates in the renal pelvis; no additional common direct organ involvement is established.
Acute mixed-phenotype leukemia involves hematopoietic blasts and marrow; the lymphoma ancestor does not change its leukemia identity.
LGI1-antibody autoimmune limbic encephalitis; intrinsic SIADH-associated hyponatremia occurs in roughly 60%. Associated tumors are separate diseases.
Defective vitamin D activation causes mineral abnormalities and defining rachitic bone disease; a hepatic enzyme defect does not establish liver injury.
Acute sarcoidosis defined by erythema nodosum and ankle arthritis/periarthritis with hilar lymphadenopathy; hilar nodes alone do not establish pulmonary tissue damage.
Anxiety is a psychiatric condition without established organ damage; neurological ancestry and SLC6A4 association do not justify a neurologic label.
